title: SONA: Learning Conditional, Unconditional, and Matching-Aware Discriminator
claim: Prior discriminators entangle or conflate authenticity and condition alignment; ours separates them into independent axes with dedicated objectives.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right (a,b prior; c ours), shared legend table bottom-right
description: Three side-by-side geometric sketches show how discriminators score samples in a gray data-space disk (R^D) holding pink (real/fake positive) and blue (negative) circles and triangles. Panel (a) AC-GAN projects samples onto separate alignment and naturalness axes, with a classifier loss V_CE and a GAN loss V_GAN. Panel (b) PD-GAN projects onto a single conditional-likelihood axis with V_GAN. Panel (c) SONA, the proposed method, uses orthogonal alignment and naturalness axes. It adds the objectives V_SAN, V_BT-c (purple) and V_BT-m (green), shown as rounded capsules with arrows pushing points apart. A legend table at the bottom right maps the marker shapes and colors to real versus fake and to positive versus negative. The eye goes first to the colorful point clusters and the capsules on the axes.
caption: Comparison of \ours with existing classifier- and projection-based methods for discriminator optimization. Our approach enables independent assessment of sample naturalness and alignment, supported by the proposed inductive bias ([ref]) and objectives ([ref]).
abstract: Deep generative models have made significant advances in generating complex content, yet conditional generation remains a fundamental challenge. Existing conditional generative adversarial networks often struggle to balance the dual objectives of assessing authenticity and conditional alignment of input samples within their conditional discriminators. To address this, we propose a novel discriminator design that integrates three key capabilities: unconditional discrimination, matching-aware supervision to enhance alignment sensitivity, and adaptive weighting to dynamically balance all objectives. Specifically, we introduce Sum of Naturalness and Alignment (SONA), which employs separate projections for naturalness (authenticity) and alignment in the final layer with an inductive bias, supported by dedicated objective functions and an adaptive weighting mechanism. Extensive experiments on class-conditional generation tasks show that \ours achieves superior sample quality and conditional alignment compared to state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, we demonstrate its effectiveness in text-to-image generation, confirming the versatility and robustness of our approach.
